summary: All four requested scenarios were driven through running product executables using isolated homes and claims; remote reply capture and application used authenticated real OpenSSH and the real remote entrypoint and job worker.

scope.transport: Dedicated unprivileged loopback sshd with worktree-local disposable host/client keys, strict pinned host verification, no global SSH configuration changes, no production credentials
scope.remote_actor: Dedicated synthetic mate whose append-only log was written by separate authenticated SSH sessions, not an LLM mate or an existing production mate
scope.worker: Real remote job worker using FM_REMOTE_JOB_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=Linux and a worktree-local FM_REMOTE_JOB_STATE_ROOT to avoid touching macOS LaunchAgents; native LaunchAgent provisioning was not tested
scope.code: Primary executables from the target worktree; remote executables copied from git archive HEAD into an isolated tracked code root, because remote root/home must not overlap
scope.boundaries: No production homes, mate records, permissions, credentials, shared configuration, packages, or LaunchAgents were modified; no linters or broad test suites were run

scenarios.name: Claim confirmation while a source lock remains contended
scenarios.observed: reconciled: published=0 started=2 stopped=0 uncertain=0 failed=0; lock-free observation confirmed pid 72701 live while the claim's source lock was held; list subsequently showed both sources live; no launch-failure episode existed
scenarios.construction: Real /bin/sleep long-poll sources, real source locks held by independent processes; planted pacing stamp and 20-second launch floor keep the claim as the only confirmation signal

scenarios.name: Unreadable claim remains uncertain rather than confirming ownership
scenarios.observed: Malformed serialized claim produced lock-free observation rc=2; reconcile started=0 uncertain=1 failed=0; list reported uncertain and the claim's original bytes were preserved
scenarios.construction: Unreadable means an invalid/truncated serialized claim, not a permission-denied file; no production permissions were changed

scenarios.name: Unstartable source cleans up and closes its failure episode after repair
scenarios.evidence: scenarios.log, SCENARIO 3 through PASS scenario 3; initial-state/failure/state/.wake-queue
scenarios.observed: An isolated registration with no executable argv yielded exit 1 and failed=1, a durable launch-failed wake and episode, but no claim, runner record, or staged output; public re-registration repaired it, then reconcile started=1 failed=0 and removed the failure episode

scenarios.name: SSH remote reply claims, captures, mirrors, acknowledges and re-arms
scenarios.observed: Two separate SSH-appended replies each produced a claim and a durable captured result and handled marker; parent status contained exactly two mirrored lines, the remote log retained exactly two original lines, the fetched markdown document was byte-identical, the cursor advanced to 118 bytes, the source re-registered after each reply, each reconcile reported started=1 failed=0, and no launch-failure episode existed

verification_failures.cause: Evidence-driver assertion error: wait_path used -s for an intentionally zero-byte handled marker, although the product had already captured, mirrored, and acknowledged the first reply
verification_failures.fix: Observe marker existence with -e; rerun only scenario 4

verification_failures.cause: Evidence-driver lifecycle error: its sole second reconcile ran before the previous capturing runner released its claim, so it correctly reported started=0; unlike a live watcher, the driver had no later periodic cycle
verification_failures.fix: Wait for the previous claim's release before the next watcher-equivalent reconcile and require started=1; focused scenario 4 re-verification exited 0

source_changes: None required: target product behavior passed. Only transient evidence-driver assertions were corrected, and their final executable driver and transport wrapper are attached as evidence.
commands: bash -x .no-mistakes/live-reply-isolation/drive-live.sh > scenarios.log 2>&1 (scenarios 1-3 passed; scenario 4 exposed an evidence-driver assertion error)
bash -x .no-mistakes/live-reply-isolation/drive-live.sh remote > remote-reverify.log 2>&1 (first reply passed; exposed an evidence-driver lifecycle error)
bash -x .no-mistakes/live-reply-isolation/drive-live.sh remote > remote-pass.log 2>&1 (exit 0, both reply generations passed)
cleanup: Each driver invocation swept only its four isolated homes and stopped its dedicated remote worker tree; the dedicated sshd and remaining transient files are retired separately, with cleanup.log recording final verification. Disposable private keys are not attached.
